hard_gates.gate: G1 tenant isolation: critic's own attack on the real product (API, DB role, exports, headers, new /api/audit/actors)
hard_gates.evidence: attack/attack-audit.mjs and .out: 903 requests as Al Noor's admin against Gulf Steel. They used B's change, record and user ids on /api/audit/log/{id} and /api/audit/records/{id} (bare, ?type= for 5 kinds, ?before=), the recordId and actorId filters (B's 100 users as actorId), search, record contains, the new /api/audit/actors (B's e-mails, e-mail domain 'gulfsteel', ids, X-Tenant-Id/X-Tenant/X-Workspace headers), and the CSV/XLSX export. Answers: 723 x 200, 120 x 400, 60 x 404, no 5xx. All 53 text matches were names or seeded file names that exist in both tenants. verify-hits.mjs checked them: all 827 matching rows belong to tenant A, and B gets 404 for each. DB as erp_app (attack/db-app.out): with no tenant bound it sees 0 rows; bound to B it sees only B's 9,102. INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE and TRUNCATE on audit.entries are all refused. Calling audit.capture() and attaching it to a temp table are refused. A row moved to B's tenant_id is refused by row-level security. All 27 tables carrying the capture trigger have forced row-level security and a tenant_id (attack/db-role.out). The one tenant table without the trigger is identity.sign_in_attempts.

biggest_gap.title: Record history and the audit log show stored codes instead of the field's labels, so the Arabic history shows English words ('sharjah → dubai', 'person')
biggest_gap.detail: The verdict is BLOCKED only because neither full verify passed every test. Each run had one load-sensitive failure outside p07's code: the p01 harness's X16 in run 1, and p16's contact-search timing budget in run 2 (see hard_gates). The product gap that most holds p07 back is how values are shown. A field that stores a code is shown as the raw code everywhere p07 shows values: the history panel (Alt+Y), the line under the record's heading, the log's 'Old and new values' column and the export. Examples are a contact's emirate (sharjah, dubai), its type (person, organisation) and country (AE). A user working in Arabic sees 'الإمارة sharjah dubai' and 'النوع person' in the history. The contacts list on the same screen shows the type as 'شخص'. AuditTexts maps choice labels only for the kinds registered in its lookup (AuditTrailTests.A_choice_shows_the_chosen_options_label... checks numbering.sequences 'reset' and asserts that contacts.contacts keeps the raw value). For a UAE trading company the emirate and contact type are everyday fields, and Odoo's chatter shows the selection label. Fix: take the labels in both languages from each list definition's column choices (the same choices the list and form already show), for every audited kind.
biggest_gap.evidence: browser/history-emirate.out. attack/emirate.mjs changes contact 'Shamma Waleed Al Romaithi' from sharjah to dubai as admin, then `node browser/walk1.mjs ar` (Ctrl+K, the contact, Alt+Y) prints the history 'الإمارة sharjah dubai' and, in the creation entry, 'النوع person', 'الدولة AE', 'الإمارة sharjah'. `node browser/walk1.mjs en` prints 'Emirate sharjah dubai'. ar-02-history-panel.jpg shows the list cell 'شخص' beside the panel. The contact was restored afterwards (emirate.mjs restore).

The stage says it measures 'alone, after every other stage', but in a critic's slot verify it shares the machine with another verify (load 6 to 12 here). Fixed since round 4 and kept fixed: (1) 'Changed by' is now a person picker (/api/audit/actors) that works by keyboard in English and Arabic. Filtering by Mariam Al Mansoori then Contact then Job title narrowed 760,186 rows to 17, 2 and 1, at 11 to 53 ms per request. (2) Tamper evidence: erp_app lost INSERT and the capture trigger is the only writer. (3) The export 'Fields' column has names, not a count, in English and Arabic (attack/export-*.csv). (4) Sign-in session times are formatted dates. (5) The line under the heading shows both the standard and the custom field change of one save. (6) The Fields filter has 160 to 161 choices and no duplicate labels.

Scope otherwise present in a real Chromium, by keyboard, in English and Arabic RTL. The history panel (Alt+Y, Escape gives focus back) works on all 12 main forms reached by G+letter: users, roles, companies, branches, company access, currencies, exchange rates, document numbering, jobs, job schedules, contacts and workspace (browser/forms.mjs). The log holds 760,000+ rows, opens in 250 ms, and filters by person, record type, field, record search and date (From only, typed as mm/dd/yyyy into a date input). Filtered CSV, XLSX and PDF exports take 250 to 400 ms in both languages. Custom field changes are captured field by field in the same transaction as the record change.

The new /api/audit/actors gives any holder of audit.log.read the names (English and Arabic) of every user in the workspace, here 100,000, even without identity.users.read. A 'Roles auditor' whose own log holds 5 rows lists people page by page (attack/perms.out, 'auditor actors empty search'). The endpoint map says this was reviewed, and e-mails are withheld. Still, it reveals more than the rows the reader may see; offering only people who appear as actors in visible rows would close it.

Person picker: the exact name does not rank first. In Arabic, 'فاطمة الزعابي' is the 4th option, after 'آنا فاطمة الزعابي' and others, because options are sorted alphabetically among contains-matches. In English, typing a first name ('Mariam') among 100,000 users never shows the admin. The picker sends one request per keystroke with no debounce.
The Arabic export's 'Changed by' column carries English names ('Fatima Al Zaabi'), while the Arabic screen shows 'فاطمة الزعابي' (attack/export-ar.csv).

Dates inside values stay ISO ('2026-12-31' for the Credit review date custom field) in the history, the heading line, the log and the export, in both languages. The owner asked for dd/mm/yyyy (decision #47).
Exporting the whole log stops at 200,000 of 760,198 rows, with a notice row (CSV 57 MB in 15 s). This is unchanged since round 2.

The history panel and the log need audit.log.read. The demo's 'Company manager' role (9 permissions) does not hold it, so a manager sees no history on any form they manage. This is unchanged since round 2.
